title: Failed remote build context leaks its temporary directory
body:
### Issue Description


When buildah build fails fetching a remote build context (e.g. from Git or HTTP) it leaves behind an empty directory in `$TMPDIR` (on Linux and Unix it's set to `/tmp`).

The reason for that is in `ForURL` (`pkg/tmpdir/url.go`). `tempDir` is used in the deferred function but it's being set to empty string in the return statement before the deferred function is called.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Here is a Bash script to reproduce this:

```bash
TMP_DIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"

count_dirs() {
    find "$TMP_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'buildah*' | wc -l
}

before=$(count_dirs)
echo "Buildah temp dirs before: $before"

echo "Running build with a nonexistent remote context..."
buildah build https://example.com/does-not-exist.tar.gz || true

after=$(count_dirs)
echo "Buildah temp directories after:  $after"
echo "Did not delete: $((after - before))"
```

### Describe the results you received

The build fails as expected, but the temporary context directory (and its `download/` subdirectory) stays on disk.

### Describe the results you expected

the temporary directory is removed
